questions.q: What should we do / is a matter of / our own choice / and desire.
o: What should we do
is a matter of
our own choice
and desire
questions.s: Explanation:- Yeh koi question nahi hai isliye interrogative structure ka nahi assertive structure ka use hoga Subject ke baad verb aayegi isliye yahan 'what we should do' ka use hoga na ki 'what should we do' ka.

questions.q: My older brother, / which you'll / meet later, / is a dentist. (SSC CGL Tier-01 12/04/22)
questions.s: 'Which' refers to objects. For a person ('brother'), the relative pronoun 'whom' should be used.

questions.q:
Although people had been on watch and/the watchkeepers were very tired,/everyone were up and buzzing.

(SSC CHSL Tier-01 15/03/23)
o: Although people had been on watch and
questions.s:
The correct answer is Option 3: Everyone were up and buzzing.

The subject "everyone" is singular, so it should be followed by the singular form of the verb "was" instead of "were".

Correct sentence: Although people had been on watch and the watchkeepers were very tired, everyone was up and buzzing.

questions.q:
We ordered a Pizza / which are one of my favourite foods.

[CGL Pre 13/04/2022 S3]
o: which are one of
questions.s:
Correct Answer: which are one of

  • "Pizza" is singular, but "are" is plural, which creates a mismatch.

  • The verb "are" should be replaced with "is" to match the singular subject "Pizza."

  • Corrected Sentence: We ordered a Pizza which is one of my favourite foods.

questions.q: Each of the students has their own desk in the classroom.
questions.s:
If the sentence starts with each of/either of/neither of, each, either, neither, ‘the’ is used before the plural noun/ plural pronoun but a singular adjective singular verb, and singular pronoun are used in the latter part of the sentence.

So, the corrected sentence is: "Each of the students has his own desk in the classroom."

questions.q:
There is no one else in this house, I can feel the presence.

(SSC MTS Tier-01 22/10/21)
questions.s:
"no one else" creates a contradiction because if there's no one, you wouldn't be able to feel someone's presence.

So, we use "someone else" to indicate that there is, in fact, another person, and that's why you can feel their presence.

Correct sentence: There is someone else in this house, I can feel the presence.

questions.q:
The thin wire that giving off light is called the filament.

[MTS 25/07/2022 S3]
questions.s:
Corrected Sentence: The thin wire that gives off light is called the filament.

"that giving off light" is incorrect because "giving" is a present participle and cannot act as the main verb of the clause.

The verb "gives" should be used to correctly complete the clause "that gives off light."

In relative clauses (starting with "that"), a finite verb ( "gives") is required to match the subject "that" (referring to the wire).

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.


He lived on the bank of a mighty river, broad and deep, that have always silently rolling on to a vast undiscovered ocean.

[CHSL TIER -I 2024]
questions.s:
The correct answer is: "which was always silently rolling"

The subject of the sentence, "a mighty river," is singular, so the verb should be "was" (singular) instead of "were" or other options.

"Which" is used to refer to things, and here it correctly refers to the river.

The correct sentence should be: "He lived on the bank of a mighty river, broad and deep, which was always silently rolling on to a vast undiscovered ocean.”

questions.q: Q20. <u>The woman is waiting to see you looks rather angry.</u>
o: C) The woman who is waiting to see you looks rather angry
A) The women whose waiting to see you looks rather angry
B) The women who is waiting see you looks rather angry
questions.s: A relative pronoun 'who' is needed to introduce the subordinate clause correctly. Option C provides the necessary structure.

questions.q: Often it makes one wonder at the sights you see,
questions.s: (a) Explanation:- one wonder at the sights one sees. yhan wonder verb ka subject one hai to obviously sights ko dekhne wala bhi one hi hai. aur one ke baad verb singular aati hai.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I find that/ I get myself tired/ very easily/ these days.
questions.s: The given sentence is grammatically incorrect. In the given sentence, 'I get tired' should be used instead of 'I get myself tired'. The use of the reflexive pronoun ‘myself’ is irrelevant according to the grammatical context of the sentence so it will be removed.

questions.q: Q6. I had to hold on (a)/to the wall (b)/to steady itself (c)/or I could have fallen. (d)
o: A) I had to hold on (a)
D) or I could have fallen. (d)
questions.s: The subject is 'I', so the reflexive pronoun should match the subject. 'Itself' should be replaced with 'myself'.

questions.q: Q5. Q5. Who (a)/ do you wish (b)/to see? (c)/No error (d) [CDS-I (2023)]
questions.s: 'Wish' क्रिया के object की ज़रूरत है, इसलिए subjective case 'Who' के स्थान पर objective case 'Whom' का प्रयोग होगा।

questions.q: Q24. Q24. He, you and I (a)/ need to prepare the final report (b)/ before the meeting scheduled next Monday morning. (c)/ No error (d)
o: (b) need to prepare the final report
(c) before the meeting scheduled next Monday morning.
questions.s: The correct order of pronouns for a general statement is 2-3-1 (Second person, Third person, First person). It should be "You, he and I".

questions.q: May I know (1)/ to who (2)/ I am speaking ? (3)/ No error. (4)
questions.s:
After a preposition like “to”, we use the objective case of the pronoun → “whom,” not “who.”
So it should be: “to whom I am speaking”

questions.q: It was ( her ) who first saw the criminal. [CHSL TIER -I 2024]
questions.s:
After a linking verb like “was,” the pronoun must be in the subjective case.
So, “It was she who first saw the criminal” is correct — not “her,” which is objective.

questions.q: The dictator (a) / himself declared (b) / all powerful. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: Need reflexive or object pronoun. Change to "declared himself" - reflexive pronoun after verb when subject and object are same.

questions.q:
In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option.

In many ways, she (A)/ was a reluctant heroine of the Mutiny, (B)/ whom happened to be at (C)/ the wrong place at the right time. (D)
questions.s:
Part C has an error.

In the given sentence, 'she' is the subject of the sentence. The relative pronoun 'whom' refers to the object of a sentence. So, its use is grammatically incorrect in the given sentence. 'Whom' should be replaced with the relative pronoun 'who' to rectify the given sentence. 'Who' is used to refer to the subject of a sentence.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: In many ways, she was a reluctant heroine of the Mutiny, who happened to be at the wrong place at the right time.

questions.q: Me and my friends / often go / to the cinema / together.
o: to the cinema
often go
Me and my friends
questions.s: Explanation:- Yahan do changes karne padenge, ek toh yeh General sentence hai isliye Pronoun ka sequence '231' use karna tha, aur dusra hume yahan subjective case ki zarurat hai isliye 'me' nahi 'I' aana tha isliye yahan par my friend and I ka use kiya jayega.

questions.q: I am sorry of which my mother said.
questions.s:
(a) Explanation:- Jab aap jiske cheez ke ke liye maafi mangte ho to uss case me 'sorry for ' ka use hota hai.

ex. I am sorry for my bad behaviour.

yhan meaning ye dena hai ki mai maffi chahunga jo meri maa ne kha tha uske liye.

yani yhan koi antecedent nhi hai isliye 'what'relative pronoun ka use hoga.

Note :- 'what my mother said' ye pura noun clause 'for' preposition ka object bnega.

questions.q: They each listened carefully to what each other said.
questions.s: (c) Explanation:- yhan verb listened hai na ki talked iss se clear hai ki ek time me ek hi person bola hoga baaki sab sun rhe honge. isliye each other ka use nhi hoga kyuki apas me baat nhi ho rhi hai. ek ne jo bola wo dusre se dhyan se suna iss meaning ke liye 'what the other said' ka use hoga.

questions.q: Q10. Q10. She is the professor (a)/ whom research students often admire her (b)/ because all her publications have been internationally recognized. (c)/ no error (d)
o: (b) whom research students often admire her
(c) because all her publications have been internationally recognized.
questions.s: The correct relative pronoun to show possession/relationship here is "whose" (i.e., whose research students...). "Whom" is incorrect in this context.

questions.q: Q15. Q15. No matter what that the mother did the baby didn't stop crying. [SSC CHSL 17/03/2020 Shift-III]
questions.s: 'What' खुद एक relative pronoun है, इसके साथ 'that' का प्रयोग करना redundant (अनावश्यक) है।

questions.q: Q7. Q[50]. The trees ______ grow here are very tall. [NDA 2022]
questions.s: 'Which' for plants/nature. पौधों और प्रकृति के लिए 'which' का प्रयोग होता है।
